messages.author: 5f950c9713997d19
messages.subject: TMB install in LInux Mint 19.3
parts:
Hi, I have encountered difficulty installing R (from source) and TMB on Linux Mint 19.3 (latest release). Specifically, I 
  • downloaded the R source tarfile from the R CRAN and untared in a subdirectory of home
  • used the Software Sources utility to add the following source repos to the sources.list.d directory (Mint's way of doing this)

    • deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu bionic-cran35/

    • ppa:marutter/c2d4u

  • executed 
    • sudo apt build-dep r-base (to install r-base dependencies)
    • ./configure -enable-R-shlib
    • make
    • make check (all good)
    • sudo make install
The R install looked OK. Then I ran the TMB simple regression example (attached) in R Studio. 

I got a huge number of warning messages, a sample of which is below, and then the final message indicating that the compile worked! The messages relate to accessing the installed TMB and RcppEigen subdirectories. Running the model indicated that it worked and produced the expected output. hmm....

Not clear at all what is going on. I thought that it might be something with the $PATH but the warning messages indicate that these directories are being accessed. Has anyone enountered this problem and can suggest a fix?

Bob

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: TMB install in LInux Mint 19.3
parts:
These warnings show up when installing any R package that depend on RcppEigen. It's a mystery to me why no one care to fix this. Anyway, it's a known problem with a known 'solution':

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/277

In short you have to tell the compiler that the warnings (hopefully) are harmless by adding to your ~/.R/Makevars something like:

EIGEN_SHUT_UP=-Wno-aggressive-loop-optimizations -Wno-deprecated-declarations -Wno-ignored-attributes -Wno-enum-compare -Wno-int-in-bool-context
CXXFLAGS+=$(EIGEN_SHUT_UP)

<http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/code/rcpp/> say:

One additional and recent change was the accom[m]odation of a recent
CRAN Policy change to not allow gcc or clang to mess with diagnostic
messages. A word of caution: this may make your compilation of packages
using RcppEigen very noisy so consider adding -Wno-ignored-attributes to
the compiler flags added in your ~/.R/Makevars.
